title: AI for Excel and Google Sheets: What Actually Works in 2026

scenes.badge: Google's claim for Fill with Gemini in Sheets
scenes.sub: Faster than typing by hand (Google study, Apr 2026)
scenes.text: Google says its new Fill with Gemini feature in Sheets can enter data nine times faster than typing it by hand. That number comes from Google's own study of ninety five people filling a hundred cells. Meanwhile, Microsoft quietly killed the Excel AI formula it announced last year, before it ever fully launched. So what actually works in spreadsheets right now? In this video, I'll show you what AI can do in Excel and Google Sheets in late twenty twenty six, four jobs worth handing over, and the limits nobody mentions.

scenes.title: AI in your spreadsheets
scenes.sub: Excel and Google Sheets: what works, what doesn't
scenes.text: Spreadsheets are where a lot of office hours disappear. Cleaning messy lists, sorting feedback, writing formulas you only half remember, building the same report every month. AI can now help with all of that inside the tools you already use. But the features, the names and the plans change fast, so everything here was checked against Google and Microsoft pages in November twenty twenty six. I'll cover both apps fairly, and I'll tell you where each one falls short, so you can decide what's worth your time.

First, a change you may have missed. In August twenty twenty five, Microsoft announced an equals COPILOT function, an AI formula you could type straight into an Excel cell. It was tested by preview users for about a year. Then Microsoft announced that starting September fourteenth, twenty twenty six, the function is no longer available. It never reached a full public launch. Microsoft says you get the same help, like summarizing, classifying, generating content and pulling info from the web, through the Copilot side pane instead. So if a tutorial tells you to type equals COPILOT, it's out of date.

scenes.chapterTitle: Copilot in Excel: plans and 3 modes
scenes.text: So what does Copilot in Excel need today? On the home side, it's included with Microsoft three sixty five Personal, Family and Premium, and on Family only the subscription owner gets it. Businesses need a Copilot plan on top. Your file has to be saved to OneDrive with AutoSave on. Copilot then works in three modes. Edit changes the workbook directly. Plan writes out the steps first so you can review them. And Chat just answers questions without touching your data. If you're nervous about AI editing a real file, Plan mode is the one to start with.

On the Google side, there are three features. The AI function is a formula: you type equals AI, then a prompt in quotes, and optionally a cell range for it to read. Fill with Gemini lets you fill one example cell, then drag down and let it complete the column. And Gemini in the side panel can build a whole formatted sheet from a description. Google lists these for Business Standard and Plus, Enterprise Standard and Plus, and personal Google AI Pro and Ultra plans. One limit to know: the AI function generates only the first three hundred fifty selected cells at a time.

items.text: Put the comments in one column

footer.text: A label is a guess, not a fact

scenes.text: Job one: sorting text into categories. Say you have five hundred customer comments in column A. In Sheets you could write equals AI, classify this review as positive, negative or mixed, and point it at cell A two. Then fill it down. In Excel, you'd open Copilot and ask it to add a column that labels each comment the same way. Either way, you get a first pass in minutes instead of reading every line yourself. Then you check a sample, because a label is a guess, not a fact.

items.text: Describe the result in plain English
Name the sheet and the columns
Ask it to explain the formula
Let real formulas do the math

footer.text: AI writes the formula. The formula does the math.

scenes.text: Job two: formulas. This might be the most useful one for beginners. Instead of searching forums for the right lookup formula, describe the result in plain English. For example: in column D, show the price from the Products sheet that matches the product name in column B. Then, and this is the important part, ask the AI to explain the formula line by line. You learn how it works, and you can spot it if it picked the wrong column. Microsoft's own guidance said its AI formula wasn't meant for numerical calculations, so let real formulas do the math.

footer.text: Google: 9x faster on a 100-cell task (its own study)

scenes.text: Job three: filling in columns from examples. Fill with Gemini is built for this. Type one or two finished examples, like a product description turned into a short title, or a customer complaint with a suggested reply next to it. Then drag down, and Gemini follows the pattern for the rest. Google tested it with ninety five people on a hundred cell task and says it was nine times faster than typing by hand. That's Google's own study, so treat it as a best case. But the idea is solid: you show the pattern once, and the AI repeats it.

scenes.chapterTitle: Job 4: Build a whole sheet or dashboard
scenes.badge: Gemini's success rate on real-world spreadsheet tasks
scenes.text: Job four: building a whole sheet or dashboard. In Sheets, you can ask Gemini for something like: add scorecards and bar charts above my sales data. It writes a plan, you approve it, and it builds the formatted sheet, with pivot tables, formulas and charts. Google reports a seventy point four eight percent success rate on a public test of real world spreadsheet tasks called SpreadsheetBench. That's impressive, but flip it around: roughly three tasks in ten still don't come out right. And for now, Google says this works in the US, in English only.

items.desc: Sees only the range you give it

items.name: Text only
items.desc: Outputs are text, not live numbers

items.name: No nesting
items.desc: You can't put it inside an IF

items.name: Manual refresh
items.desc: Changed inputs may not update outputs

items.name: Usage caps
items.desc: Hit the long one, wait up to 24 hours

scenes.text: Now the limits, straight from Google's help page. The AI function can't see your whole spreadsheet or other files, only the range you give it. It returns text only. You can't put it inside another formula, like an IF. If the inputs change, some outputs won't refresh by themselves, so you refresh them. And there are short and long term usage limits. Hit the long one and you may wait twenty four hours. Excel's home plans have usage limits too. Neither app promises the answers are correct, and Google says not to rely on it for financial or legal advice.

scenes.chapterTitle: 4 rules before AI touches a real file

items.text: Read the plan before you approve
Keep money math in normal formulas

footer.text: You sign off on the numbers

scenes.text: So here are four rules worth following before AI touches a real spreadsheet. One: work on a copy, never the only version. Two: in Excel, start in Plan mode, and in Sheets, read Gemini's plan before you approve it. Three: spot check at least ten rows by hand, including the weird ones, like blanks and typos. Four: keep money math, totals and anything you'll report in normal formulas you can audit. AI is great at the boring setup work. You're still the one who signs off on the numbers.

scenes.chapterTitle: Excel or Sheets: which to use

big.sub: Don't buy a plan just for this

footer.text: No plan? Paste a small, non-sensitive sample into a free chatbot

scenes.text: So which one should you use? If your work already lives in Excel and you have Microsoft three sixty five Personal, Family or Premium, open the Copilot pane and start with Chat and Plan modes. If you live in Google Sheets on an eligible Workspace or Google AI plan, the AI function and Fill with Gemini are the quickest wins, because they work right inside the cells. If you have neither plan, don't buy one just for this. Try the free version of any AI chat assistant. Paste a small, non sensitive sample and ask it to write the formula for you.

scenes.title: A fast assistant, not an accountant
scenes.next: The 50/30/20 Budget Rule Explained with Real Numbers
scenes.text: So, AI in spreadsheets is real and useful in late twenty twenty six, but it's a fast assistant, not an accountant. Use it to sort text, write and explain formulas, fill patterns and draft dashboards. Then check its work, and keep the important math in formulas you control. Now I want to hear from you. What's the one spreadsheet task you'd hand to AI first? Tell me in the comments. If this helped, subscribe to Future Money Lab, and I'll see you in the next video.

youtube.title: AI for Excel and Google Sheets: What Actually Works in 2026
youtube.summary: What can AI really do in Excel and Google Sheets right now? I researched Microsoft's and Google's own pages (checked November 2026): why Excel's =COPILOT function was retired before it ever launched, how Copilot in Excel works today (Edit, Plan and Chat modes), Google's three Gemini features in Sheets (the AI function, Fill with Gemini and building whole sheets from a prompt), four jobs worth handing to AI, five limits most tutorials skip, and four rules before AI touches a real spreadsheet.
youtube.details:
Facts mentioned (checked November 2026):
- Excel's =COPILOT function was a preview feature (Insider/Frontier); Microsoft announced it in August 2025 and says it is no longer available beginning September 14, 2026. The Copilot side pane offers the same kinds of help: summarizing, classifying, generating content and retrieving information from the web (Microsoft 365 message center MC1454373, Aug 13, 2026; TechRadar, Aug 17, 2026).
- Microsoft said the function was not meant for numerical calculations (as reported by TechRadar).
- Copilot in Excel on home plans: Microsoft 365 Personal, Family (subscription owner only) and Premium; business users need a Copilot plan; files must be saved to OneDrive with AutoSave on; modes Edit, Plan and Chat; home plans have usage limits (Dupple guide citing Microsoft pages, Nov 2026).
- Google Sheets AI function: =AI("prompt", [range]); text output only; sees only the range you pass; can't be nested (e.g. inside IF); some outputs need a manual refresh; short- and long-term usage limits (wait 24 hours after the long-term one); only the first 350 selected cells generate per run (Google Docs Editors Help).
- Fill with Gemini: Google says it populates data 9x faster than manual entry for 100-cell tasks, based on its own study of 95 participants (Google Workspace Updates, April 22, 2026).
- Building/editing whole spreadsheets with Gemini: 70.48% success rate on the full SpreadsheetBench dataset as reported by Google; US and English only (Google Workspace Updates, April 22, 2026).
- Eligible Google plans listed: Business Standard and Plus, Enterprise Standard and Plus, AI add-ons, Google AI Pro and Ultra.
- Plans and features change often; check your own plan before you buy anything.
